The Doctor runs around the control room scanning the walls and doors with his sonic screwdriver.
So someone quite clever has created dozens of identical control rooms and has moved all of my dear friends into them.

He pauses by a door, taps it gently with the sonic screwdriver.
Found you! Life signs just on the other side of this door. Now, where is that control panel...
You have to be kidding me.
You will provide us with parts.

We can be hurt now, really hurt, the stakes were just raised.
And the virus can create any enemy you have ever met, inside any environment you've ever been to?
Everywhere I've ever been, and a few more on top. We're in real danger.
I'm assuming these things aren't friendly?
Target: The Doctor. Charge: Crimes untold. Plea: Guilty. Sentence: Execution!

There's nothing we can do. They're more than capable of handling themselves.
If someone has done this to them... let's just say that I wouldn't like to be the one up against those thirteen.
We need to push forward into the library, we have a job to do.
And without a beat the older ''Professor'' River Song was leading us,
Walking out the doors of the TARDIS, issuing orders and warnings.  The leader we needed.
I hope the Doctor has prepared you all. I hope you're all ready for what we're about to face.

407.id: As we head towards the vault, make sure you keep out of the shadows.
This whole planet is infested with a creature called the Vashta Nerada.
We can't hurt them in their normal state, but I may be able to give us some leverage.
Follow me and stay close, I know exactly where we can find the book we need.
This library is the size of a planet, it contains every single book ever written, and it has a very special room just for the Doctor.
The Vashta Nerada you encounter while in the library are immune to any damage while their ''shadows'' buff is active.
Use Professor River Song's ''Illuminate'' ability to temporarily remove the shadows so you can do damage to the Vashta Nerada and get through the Library.

408.id: You at the back, no dallying!

409.id: Keep close, we need to keep moving towards that book. Move! Move! Move!

410.id: We're almost at the Doctor's vault!
Hey, who turned out the lights?

411.id: A lonely TT capsule, Type 40, Mark 3 TARDIS sits in the time vortex, gently spinning in the silence of infinity.
As time collapses around them, the 13 incarnations of the Doctor and dozens of his most faithful, determined allies find themselves having a rare moment to catch their breath.
In the distance--too quick and too small to be picked up by early warning protocols--a thin, glowing lance of metal shoots towards the TARDIS at inhuman speeds.
Their moment of silence is about to be shattered by an old acquaintance...

412.id: So, go on then, ask me.
No.
Go on! This is fun! Admit it!
This isn't remotely fun.
Go on! Ask me. Ask me how I would deal with a Royal Beast of Peladon while in a...
Where this time? Is this the only way you can relax while the TARDIS refuels?
In a garlic factory!
Yours is almost as bad as mine.
Leave them be, it's good to be prepared. You never know what could be around the next...
The 8th Doctor senses something and looks over at the central console.
A lifetime of connection to the psychic circuits of the TARDIS, a sixth sense.
He's not alone, a second later the console is crowded with his incarnations.
There's something on the scanner, but it's traveling far too fast,
Possibly some sort of controlled superlucent emission.
BATTLESTA...
Damage?
Please tell me you were about to scream "battle stations".
This is no time for...well, yes, I was.
But you're never to speak of that again. I expected it to be more...
Gallant?
Useful. Everyone, up, now. Let's see what the...
The central console sparks and screams.
damage is like.

413.id: We have to move fast. All it would take is the virus deciding to open the exterior door, flushing us out into the time vortex.
And it would be game over for not just us, but for all of reality!
The TARDIS control room lights start to flicker.
Suddenly the molecules of the TARDIS interior warp around the Doctors and their allies, the 12th Doctor's control room is replaced by...
Much better, I could never think properly in the other one. Too busy... *chuckles to himself*
The control room shifts once more, back into the 12th Doctor's version.
This is not good, not good at all. Doctor?
No need for alarm. The infinite space inside the TARDIS, every inch, every atom, is controlled by the ship.
The TARDIS's architectural reconfiguration system can make anything reality -- anything it commands this space to be, will be.
It's ok, don't panic. We're not really in The Library, we're still in the TARDIS.
She's just pulled this location from her memory banks, the virus is making her do some very strange...
...things. Let's hope at some point we get back to the TARDIS control room.

414.id: The TARDIS architectural reconfiguration system is cross referencing her memory streams, building places she's been.
And, oh boy, has she been to some very dark and scary places.
She's being forced to create a replica of her own grave, she must be terrified. We have to stop this now.
Doctor!
As the lights of the TARDIS dim, the Doctor will atone for his sin.
Stand back! I have faced these creatures before and for the glory of the Sontaran Empire I will do so again!
Behind me Jenny!
Where are these things coming from?
You thought the TARDIS could only create furniture? She's much smarter, and more deadly, than that.
As the whispermen vanish in a cloud of reclaimed molecules the world around the Doctor starts to corrupt.
What's happening now?
The virus, it's flooding through the TARDIS core systems, corrupting everything as it goes. As well as overriding the architect systems,
The virus is degrading them, making them unable to build the world around us at the fidelity we are used to.
Truly astounding. This vehicle of yours never ceases to amaze me, Doctor.
That's better...mostly.
The incarnations of the Doctor rush to the control panel to try to control the damage the virus is doing to the TARDIS systems.
A fierce look of determination on their faces.
A piercing scream rings out through the control room, a final plea for help.
She's got nothing left. Her systems are riddled with the virus.
She won't be able to help us much longer.

415.id: The 10th Doctor frantically uses controls on the central console.
We need to try and secure some of her data streams, we must contain the damage in any way we can.
Oh my God! Doctor, what's happening to you?
(Looks down at himself) I don't know, what's happening to me?
I mean, how you look is all corrupted. Pixelated.
Careful old man, you don't look any better.
The TARDIS can project anything onto your visual cortex, and the system controlling that has been invaded by the virus.
We're all still the same, but the TARDIS is making us look this way to each other.
Hmmmm. Making people you see look really strange, maybe the virus was created by the Trickster Brigade to mess with us.
I'm still me, you're still you, there are far more important things to be worried about right now.
With a final scream the consciousness of the TARDIS loses control of her core systems.
The lights in the control room go dark.
"If any of you feel a door handle, don't turn it."

417.id: Back to the door! Time to override the circuits and see who is on the other side.
He opens a panel, runs his hands over the controls lovingly.
A beep, a whir, and the door opens just as the circuit shorts out and sets fire to the Doctor's jacket.
Through the door run a relieved looking Rory Williams, and a distressed Amy Pond.
Doctor! Fire! Why are you on fire?

419.id: Ugh. Judoon. Never around when you actually need them, always around when you don't.
The control room reconfigures around Amy, Rory and the Doctor.
Interesting choice. The virus is trying to scare us, moving us into dangerous situations,
Mixing up enemies from her memory banks to confuse us. This is going to get ugly, stay close.

420.id: Elsewhere the 1st Doctor paces around his suddenly empty version of the 12th TARDIS control room.
How very interesting. Very interesting indeed.
The 1st Doctor scans the center control console, its lights dead.
He runs his hand over the surface trying to feel the subtle, reassuring vibrations of an operating machine...nothing.
The 1st Doctor looks at the floor, then starts to pace around the room with a purpose, pushing his ear up to the walls, tapping them, listening for a reply.
Ah ha! Something alive just on the other side of this divider... now, where has he hidden the door controls...
Out run Porridge, Jack Harkness and some other trapped allies.
You two, the two who look like soldiers, come over here.
Thanks for getting us out of there.
Yes. I am afraid young man that we are in some trouble indeed.
And this change of scenery is not an improvement!

422.id: Are those things the cause of the damage to the TARDIS?
No, they are cybermen, and they are not the cause of our current difficulties.
Someone, or something, has attacked my TARDIS. He or she or it has separated me from my friends and I shall not stand for it.
Let us forge a path ahead, and we shall make them pay!
Follow the rest of the story in Bigger on the Inside, Chapter 1: TARDIS under attack! Coming soon!

423.id: This room is huge! And every book has something to do with the Doctor?
Not just books it seems. All manner of literature.
There's an envelope over here from Madame de Pompadour.
As he spins through time in his TARDIS the Doctor touches billions of lives.
From ancient tales of the stranger who entered the city at night and defeated the demons with his magical stick,
Through to letters of gratitude, we'll be able to find them all here.
Spread out, everyone take a bookcase, move quickly and remember to stay out of the shadows.
What are these bottles? They're fascinating.
Not all knowledge exists in written form.
I'm really glad he's not here right now. Can you imagine just one of them let loose near these books?
He'd be bouncing off the bookcases like a pinball.
I've found it! It's a bit battered, but the front has the name Alison Docherty written on it.
Professor River Song flicks through the book before...
The book explains that the Toclafane can be short circuited by a current of 58.5 kiloamperes transferred charge of 510 megajoules precisely.
She slams the book shut and smiles.
Mission accomplished, time to head back to the TARDIS!

425.id: Quiet, I hear something. UNIT Commander, scout ahead.
The group stood and waited, nervously glancing at any shadows nearby for signs of movement.
(Whispering) Shadows that eat you? I can't imagine anything worse.
(Whispering) Robots who want to harvest your organs? They turn up far more often than I'd like.
You were right, sir, Toclafane ahead!
The Master, he's tracked us here.
Right, we're going to try something that the lads in army camp called ''The Lethbridge-Stewart'',
You find your enemy's weakness and exploit it mercilessly.
I'm assuming one of you robotic experts has the ability to reproduce Professor Docherty's experiment?
Right, let's short circuit these creatures!
Nearly back to the TARDIS. Here's hoping a group of gentlemen are there waiting for us!

426.id: We were almost back to the TARDIS when...
(Looking around) So the Doctor has finally given up, then?
Taking a little break. You know how hard that man works.
I tried, oh how I tried, to make him take a vacation from all of this "saving the universe" stuff, but he would never listen.
Clever, I can see why he chose you.
(He walks towards a nearby bookshelf, flicks his fingers across the spines)
So fitting, all your stories ending here. No need to flick to the end of the book,
"The tale of the Doctor's lost army". Everybody knows that everybody dies.
Spoilers, sweetie.
I don't care how many years you spent with him, you're a poor copy.
I never tried to be, nobody ever could be.
With no warning the Master vanished.
Escaping through space and time? Cheap.
The Doctor always had a rather low opinion of him, and now I can see why.
That may well have been true in the past...
But things change, don't they Melody? My, my, look at you all. Like...lost children.
Or a pack of adorable but ultimately gullible and disposable puppies. Remnants of a history which is about to no longer exist.
She scans around the room, her eyes lingering on Brigadier Lethbridge-Stewart.
Oh, I do like a man in a uniform!
You're not going to like this one.
Well knock me down with a feather, a rather strong temporal quake if I'm not mistaken.
Is that the Doctor knocking? Perhaps it's appropriate to end this dance here. Ta ta!
We have to get after her!
No. We have to get back to the TARDIS, nowhere else is safe.

427.id: The TARDIS doors slammed shut. With what sounded like a large and hollow "pop" The Twelfth Doctor reappeared, shocked, in the middle of the console room.
Whoa Nellie!
He pats himself all over, checking he's really all there. He points at the older River Song.
You. Hair. You're taking some serious blame for this one.
He points at the younger River.  Pushing a lever slowly down, the lights dim,
The TARDIS engines go up an octave-subtle, but the roar is so all-encompassing in the crowded control room that everyone notices and looks around.
And you, younger one, your timeline is at fault too. Now, if I can just boost the power enough...
The Eleventh Doctor appears, horizontal, several feet off the ground, and falls unceremoniously.
He wipes his jacket as he lifts himself off the ground.
I always meant to build a robot to keep this place clean. Keep boosting the power!
You're using the TARDIS to stabilize your time line?
The web of time is collapsing, and all of me being here along with both of you, given how intertwined our threads, our timelines are, they just...
The Tenth Doctor walks into the control room through an adjacent door.
The timelines just snapped, temporarily. But the TARDIS can hold everything together, at least we think she can.
One by one the incarnations of the Doctor returned, until...
There are places in space and time where the destinies of two people collide. Places that are so important that the stress they put on the web of time is incalculable.
Thirteen of me is bad enough, but being at the library with two versions of River Song... Let's just say we need to be a lot more careful in the future.
The Eleventh Doctor walks up to Professor River Song.
I looked after them, we went on a field trip to the library.
I never doubted for a second you would take care of them.
I checked out a book!
Then it's time to devise a plan. Brigadier, follow me!

428.id: While we work out a plan, perhaps we should pick up some old friends!

431.id: So you're saying that if we can find this piece of Cyberman technology, we can disable all Toclafane?
That is correct, young lady.
Wherever they are in space and time?
The Doctors seems to think so, and I don't have any reason to doubt them.
They certainly were using some big words, and gesturing a lot.
Apparently we hook this cyber-gadget into the TARDIS time circuits, or somesuch, and she will do the rest.
Every one of the Toclafane, no matter where they are in time and space, will be zapped.
Everyone gather around, we have a plan.
We need a piece of Cyberman technology, it's rare - A terullian transformer from a Cyberman info-stamp,
but there's a chance we can find it wherever we can find a Cyberman.
We should split up, cover more ground. Time may be relative, but it's still counting down.
I've had some run-ins with those horrible creatures, I'll go back to my time. Brigadier, why don't you come with me?
If you insist, Doctor.
I'm going to poke around my timeline a little. Clara, River, let's take a walk around London.
(A deeply sad look in his eyes) Cybermen always give me the shivers.
Organic matter underneath all of that... circuity and hydraulic fluid. Emotion as a weakness, metal and z-bombs.
So, will you be heading off to Antarctica then?
I never met... do you mean I meet these cyber-creatures later in my timeline?
Spoilers, sweeties.
Then if they are part of my timeline then yes, yes I must go at once.
Remember - take something gold. Cybermen aren't overly fond of gold.

432.id: Keep your eyes open, we only need one of those info-stamps!
No luck. Maybe they carry them around more in the future?

433.id: Meanwhile, elsewhere in space and time...
Lovely, lovely London. Let's find some Cybermen!
Gah, no good, I wonder how rare these things are? Let's check outside.

434.id: The twelfth incarnation of the Doctor, Clara and River Song exit the building to find...
Isn't it lovely here? I always enjoy London. I find all the negative energy and bad feelings really... rejuvenates me.
All on your own? Doesn't sound like you to wander into a fight without backup.
I'll try not to burden you with all the baggage of trying to understand what's going on around you by making this quick. Goodbye Doctor.
Missy taps buttons on a device attached to her wrist.
Oh, another paradox generator? I've been told all about that trick of yours.
Without another word Missy vanished, and the clouds above St Paul's cathedral started to bruise and swirl around a massive paradox which began to open high above the city.
No time, look at what's coming out of the cathedral!

435.id: Above the Doctor, River and Clara, the clouds gathered and spun, lightning sparking down to Earth, one fork catching Bessie.
From the doors of St. Paul's cathedral came a flood of Cybermen.
Doctor, the Cybermen have split us up from River and the others!
(Shouting to River above the overwhelming sound of metal on metal) There are too many of them, secure the TARDIS!
Doctor! I made it to the TARDIS!
The Doctor barely hears River as he stares, spellbound, at the massive rift opening over London.
Oh my... Clara, get in Bessie, NOW!

436.id: Out of the paradox came the gigantic Cyber King.
It stood, towering over London, looking down at Clara and the Doctor as they jumped into Bessie and sped away.
Its huge head panned to one side and it took its first lumbering steps, striding after the tiny yellow car.
I really need to upgrade Bessie. Who drives with manual gears anymore?
And it'll crush us like a bug if we don't keep moving!

437.id: The Cyber King's tracking system is only going to become more accurate, it's only a matter of time before something hits us!

438.id: River slams the TARDIS door behind her as she sprints to the central console.
The room echoes with the boom of a hundred cyber-fists smashing down against the TARDIS' exterior chronoplasmic shell.
No time for safety checks, we need to get off the ground and away from those cybermen!
Hold on! Taking a tight left onto Merchant Street!
Be useful and hold the wheel a sec, I have an idea!
The Doctor points his sonic screwdriver at an incoming missile which starts to spark.
And in the distance the Cyber King lets out a low, angry metallic roar.
I've managed to re-program the missile guidance system, they'll always land 20 yards to the left.
Behind Bessie an incoming rocket veers sharply to the right and explodes inside a photocopy business.
Right, left, doesn't matter as long as we're still here. Which we are.
In the distance, the Cyber King lets out a deafening, metallic roar.
I don't think he's happy with your re-programming.
They're never happy when I take away their toys.
It's backed off to repair, but it'll be back!

439.id: There's no way we can take that Cyber King on ourselves. We can do damage, but we'll never be able to stop it.
Then we have to outrun it.
The Doctor reaches below Bessie's steering wheel and pulls a lever marked "Super Drive".
I hope this still works! Hang on!
It's not enough! Every step it takes covers half a mile, it's catching up!
Soon that cyber-monstrosity will be close enough to use that huge blaster of his, we have to try and slow him down!
Well that little experiment put us 30 seconds closer to death.
Now to do something useful. Call the TARDIS, River will be there. We need her. Now.

440.id: Call the TARDIS! Call the TARDIS! How many times do I have to say that!?
Don't you lot carry mobile phones everywhere?
Well, yes. But I'm different, I use it for...
Yes, I'm sure you're nothing like the others. Selfies and likes and a frightening amount of over-sharing.
With one hand on Bessie's steering wheel he grabs Clara's mobile phone, tosses it in his lap, and uses his sonic screwdriver on it.
Do you want me to hold it? Speak to her?
What decade are you from? Bessie has hands free!
Bessie's old speakers crackle for a few seconds with static then start to ring, until...
The TARDIS residence, River Song speaking.
What do you want me to do? I'm above the city tracking you. Good driving, by the way.
It's going to take me a few minutes to disable the safeguards. Stay alive!

441.id: Just one more minute! River nearly has the TARDIS in position!
Oh no! The Cyber King has repaired its rocket control subsystem!
Stabilizers off! Hold on to something everyone!
Behind the Doctor, the TARDIS lands in front of the CyberKing with the force of an asteroid,
Cracking the earth in two, a great chasm opening up in the middle of the city.
The CyberKing tries to slow but he stumbles, end over end, downwards into the dark.
River, come pick us up. Time to get out of here.
Did you find what we needed?
Any info-stamp which may be here is probably at the bottom of that hole.
We have to get out of here, get somewhere safe. Let's hope the other me's had more luck.

467.id: We're being pulled into a rift!

488.id: As time spins around them, the various incarnations of the Master sit around their TARDIS.
So that was your big plan, was it? Crush them with a Cyber King? You truly are insane.
While we didn't end up with the flattened Doctor that I hoped for, I wouldn't call it a complete failure.
During the chase we managed to scan his TARDIS for quite a while after River shut down some of the safeguards.
And I also used the time to hunt down an old friend. I'm such a multitasker.”
Please, Missy, do enlighten us with your genius.
We've started to reverse engineer the device the Doctor is going to use against our Toclafane army.
(Sits up, suddenly caring) Who is this "we"? So now we have a way to stop the Doctor?
A movement in the shadows, Missy breaks into a sly smile.
No, but we now have a way to fight back. We wasted too many of our lives because of that man, payback is long overdue.
Doctor, I'm freezing -- does the TARDIS have a thermostat?
It has gotten a bit chilly in here, I agree.
Silurians don't function well in the cold.
Too hot, too cold, it never stops with you lot.
I never thought putting together an army to save the universe would take so much day to day micromanagement.
This is a space ship in the middle of a war, not a local seaside bed and breakfast.
The last paradox we encountered was off the Bocca scale! The web of time is dangerously close to collapsing.
(Looking at Vastra, kindly) It's all right, my dear, I'll take care of it.
Time for a counterattack -- turn on the machine!
The TARDIS is rocked by a violent storm which subsides as quickly as it appeared.
Is everyone OK?
I think so. The automatic defense mechanisms triggered correctly.
The ship's readouts show that a small amount of matter was forcefully dematerialized from various locations in the interior.
What could that possibly be about?
I can't believe it. My...
Sonic Screwdriver, it's gone!
Jack Harkness sprints into the control room.
My sonic blaster, it's gone!
My sonic lipstick has vanished as well!
I'm sure we can do without them?
We're at a huge disadvantage to the Master if we don't track them down. Anyone have any ideas?
The first doctor smiles and looks down. He starts to play with the signet ring sitting on the middle finger of his right hand.
My signet ring can perform many of the same tasks as your missing devices, however it wasn't created from the same sonic technology.
I assume this rendered it immune to the attack which put us in this situation. That puts me in an interesting position.
If you're planning on leading a team to get the sonic devices back, count me in.
And me, I've been itching for an adventure. I reckon it's time for a change of clothes.
An adventure? There's no chance you're going without me!
Or me!
Then the team is assembled. Let us start our adventure!

489.id: From the estate to here, let's go save the universe!
I've tracked down the closest sonic device. It seems to be your sonic blaster, Captain!
My old Villengard special, it'll be good to have her back.

490.id: We're getting closer, Jack's blaster should be around here somewhere...

492.id: So many devices to track down, where will we end up next I wonder?

499.id: These Toclafane appearing can't be a good sign, right Doctor?
You are correct young lady, but we must move onwards.

500.id: It's you. So you're behind the disappearance of the sonic devices!
Give up, you'll never track them all down!

504.id: You never know when to yield, do you?
I've never backed down before, and the stakes have never been greater!

516.id: We're nearly done! I wonder who's guarding the final sonic device of our adventure?
The grumpy one will not be happy if we leave this behind.

517.id: Our adventure is complete! Splendid work everyone! Time to head back to the TARDIS!

518.id: Clara! Come On! We're having an adventure!
Are all Time Lords so bossy?
Are all humans so slow? Catch up!
Don't be fooled by its appearance!

519.id: River! Where did you say you parked the TARDIS?

520.id: Ood, my old friend, I do love our strolls.

521.id: Clara, meet my old friend Jenny!
I'm so happy to meet you!

522.id: Me? What are you doing here?
Time for an adventure! Let's go collect some friends!
